extracted.intended_audience: senior-level public relations practitioners considering FPRA CPRC certification
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for earning the Florida Public Relations Association Certified Public Relations Counselor (CPRC) credential, including eligibility, written and oral exam formats, scoring rules, grading procedures, and preparation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to earn the CPRC credential, PR practitioners must have 10 years of experience, be FPRA members in good standing and have earned the APR. Once earned, the CPRC credential stays with that member as long as they maintain their membership with FPRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must verify 10 years' experience, current FPRA membership, and possession of APR before applying; maintaining FPRA membership is required to retain the credential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core competency expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: CPRC credential recognizes advanced PR counselors who have demonstrated the knowledge, skills and abilities to handle crisis situations and high stakes PR situations by thinking quickly and providing strategic PR counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should be prepared to show advanced counseling ability, especially rapid, strategic response under high-stakes or crisis conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of RPIE method
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPRC exam ... requires candidates to draw from their years of solid public relations planning, counseling and experience in applying the Research-Planning-Implementation-Evaluation (RPIE) method to solve problems and present solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both written and oral responses should apply a strategic RPIE approach and explicitly address the Research, Planning, Implementation, and Evaluation steps as relevant to each scenario.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written exam format
rubrics_metrics.description: The written exam consists of 14 case studies. Each question has an assigned length of time for answering ranging from 15 to 60 minutes. The written exam takes six hours in total to complete. This includes 2.5 hours for the first half of the exam, a required 1-hour lunch break, and 2.5 hours for the second half of the exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time management matters: the time allotted for each question also represents the number of points possible for that question (e.g., a 15-minute question is worth 15 points). Be prepared to answer multiple timed case studies in one day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written exam scoring and pass threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of points possible on the written exam is 300. To pass, a candidate must score 210 points, which is equal to 70%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to achieve at least 70% of total points (210/300) on the written portion to pass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written exam grading process
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPRC exam is peer-evaluated. Exams are graded by FPRA professionals who have earned the CPRC credential. Two CPRCs grade each exam. If both pass the candidate, the CPRC is awarded. If the graders disagree, the exam is sent to a third CPRC for grading. If the result is not a passing grade, the candidate will be asked to retake the written exam. Candidates are identified by a number, not their name, to protect their privacy. Graders are also kept confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect anonymous, peer grading by credentialed CPRCs; discrepancies are resolved by a third grader. A non-passing result requires retaking the written exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written exam content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must demonstrate persuasive counseling skills in the scenarios commonly faced by government agencies, corporations, nonprofit organizations and public relations firms. Though no two candidates’ answers on the CPRC exams will be exactly alike, successful answers apply a strategic RPIE approach and address the key elements presented in each scenario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus responses on persuasive counseling, scenario-specific key elements, and clear application of RPIE; tailor answers to the organization type in the prompt when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral exam format
rubrics_metrics.description: For the oral exam, the candidate must give a 20-minute presentation to a panel of certified evaluators, to be followed by a 10-minute question and answer session. Seven days before the scheduled presentation, the candidate will receive three fictitious scenarios ... The candidate will choose a scenario and then make their presentation, approximately 20-minutes in length, as if presenting a recommendation to the company/organization leadership as specified in the scenario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a 20-minute verbal recommendation based on one chosen scenario received a week in advance, anticipating a 10-minute Q&A from the panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral exam evaluation focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates are evaluated based on their verbal communication skills, NOT on presentation materials. Presentation materials such as PowerPoint/Prezi/etc. are not required but may be used if desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate on verbal clarity, persuasion, organization, and delivery rather than reliance on slides or handouts; materials are optional and not the basis for scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral exam scoring, criteria, and pass threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel of three FPRA professionals who have earned the CPRC credential will evaluate the presentation. Items evaluated include the specific steps of RPIE, whether the candidate was persuasive and effective and the overall impression of the judges. Each item is scored between one and five for a total of 50 points. A candidate must score 35 points (70%) or more to pass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to be scored on discrete items (RPIE steps, persuasiveness, effectiveness, overall impression) on a 1–5 scale; reach at least 70% (35/50) to pass the oral portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exam sequencing flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The exam consists of two sections: an essay-based written exam and an oral exam. They can be done in the order of the candidate’s choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates may choose whether to take the written or oral portion first based on readiness or scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and study resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Following acceptance to sit for the CPRC exam and payment of fees, candidates will be sent a digital CPRC Prep Guide. It is strongly recommended that this guide be reviewed before taking the exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official CPRC Preparation Guide and chapter Credentialing Chair support for readiness, sample questions, scheduling, and study planning.
